doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: What he tells students to listen to and his iPod
summary: Cannonball, Maceo Parker, Herbie Hancock's Bennie Maupin, Eddie Harris, Coltrane, Kenny Garrett.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: If you had students, like what would you tell them to listen to?

Cannonball I think. Well yeah, depending on what style they’re trying to get into. If they’re trying to play and trying to get some groove stuff and funk, obviously Maceo Parker. That would be one. And listen to like Herbie Hancock records for like funk. I can’t remember, I’m spacing on the name, uh the saxophone player for Herbie.
Oh yeah, I know who you mean. Now I won’t be able to think of it either. Bennie Maupin?

Yes. Bennie Maupin. Eddie Harris. Some good like groove kind of stuff, John Coltrane, not for that but, yeah. I would say Maceo, listen to Kenny Garrett. If you’re a saxophone player listen to Kenny Garrett.
Do you have a fairly extensive CD collection?

Yeah, they’re all in my iPod right now. But yeah, I have somewhere around nine thousand songs in my iPod, varying from Jimi Hendrix to Michael Jackson to Cannonball to Mozart. So it’s an all-around situation.
